issues.sym: A high-voltage battery warning. In rare cases the battery can overheat and catch fire, sometimes without warning.
issues.why: Volkswagen found that some battery packs can overheat (NHTSA 26V-030, about 43,900 vehicles). The fix is a battery software update, and a new battery where needed.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls right away and follow any charging or parking limits Volkswagen gives until the repair is done.

issues.t: High-voltage battery may fail and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A high-voltage battery warning, or in rare cases smoke or fire from under the car.
issues.why: A separate 2026 recall (NHTSA 26V-630, about 22,500 vehicles, also covering 2026 models) found the battery can fail and start a fire. The repair was still being developed when announced.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Until it's fixed, charge to no more than 80% as Volkswagen advises, and park outside if you can.

issues.t: Battery cell modules with misaligned electrodes (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The danger is a battery fire, most likely around charging.
issues.why: Some battery cell modules were built with misaligned electrodes that can short inside (NHTSA 25V-836 and 26V-028, a few hundred vehicles).
issues.next: Check the VIN. Until the modules are replaced, park outside after charging, don't charge indoors overnight, avoid DC fast charging and keep the charge at or below 80%.

issues.t: Door can open unexpectedly from wet door handle (recall)
issues.sym: Door handle error messages, a click like the locks working, or a door that unlatches by itself.
issues.why: Water can get into the electric door handles and reach the circuit board inside. Volkswagen recalled every US and Canadian ID.4 (NHTSA 24V-651, after earlier recalls 23V-312 and 23V-213).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Dealers inspect the handles, replace bad ones and update software for free. If a door misbehaves, contact a dealer right away.

issues.t: On-board charger stops charging the 12V battery (recall)
issues.sym: 12V battery warnings, the car not starting, or loss of drive power and reduced functions while driving.
issues.why: Moisture inside the on-board charger can damage a circuit board, so the 12V battery stops being charged (NHTSA 25V-125).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Dealers replace the charger unit for free.

issues.t: Sudden loss of drive power from battery software (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights and a sudden loss of power while driving.
issues.why: Software could make the battery management module restart or shut off the power inverter (NHTSA 23V-040).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Dealers update the software for free.

issues.t: Loss of power from poor battery soldering (recall)
issues.sym: A high-voltage battery warning and a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: Poor soldering on a flexible circuit inside the battery could cause an unreliable connection (NHTSA 22V-162, a few hundred early cars).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Dealers replace the affected battery modules for free.

issues.t: Screens fail to start or keep rebooting (recall)
issues.sym: The driver display or center screen stays dark or restarts, so the speedometer or backup camera image may be missing.
issues.why: A software fault can stop the displays from booting or make them reset (NHTSA 24V-344, about 80,000 vehicles).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls; dealers update the software for free.

issues.t: Gear position not shown, rollaway risk (recall)
issues.sym: The display doesn't show which gear the car is in.
issues.why: Brake control software could keep the gear indicator from displaying, so a driver might leave the car thinking it's in Park (NHTSA 25V-120).
issues.next: Always make sure the parking brake is on before getting out. Check the VIN; dealers update the software for free.

issues.sym: No picture, or a frozen picture, from the backup camera when reversing.
issues.why: Faulty cameras or camera control modules on some cars (NHTSA 22V-823 and 24V-875).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls; dealers replace the camera or module for free. Use your mirrors until it's fixed.

issues.t: 12V cable can rub through near steering column (recall)
issues.sym: Electrical warnings or a loss of drive power. A short circuit could also cause a fire.
issues.why: On some rear-drive cars, the 12V charging cable can rub against the steering column shaft until it shorts (NHTSA 22V-956).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and park outside until it's repaired. Dealers repair or replace the cable for free.

issues.t: Coolant can leak into drive motor electronics (recall)
issues.sym: Several warning lights at once and a loss of drive power.
issues.why: A motor sealing ring was fitted incorrectly on some cars, letting coolant reach the high-voltage parts (NHTSA 22V-830).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Dealers inspect the motor and replace it if needed, for free.

issues.t: Panoramic roof sunshade not flame-resistant enough (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. The shade fabric may not meet the federal flammability standard.
issues.why: The sunshade material on cars with the panoramic roof didn't meet the fire-resistance rule (NHTSA 23V-750).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls; dealers treat the shade with a flame retardant for free.

issues.t: Passenger air bag fasteners may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. The passenger air bag may not deploy correctly in a crash.
issues.why: Fasteners holding the passenger front air bag inflator may not have been tightened properly (NHTSA 24V-643).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls; dealers inspect and replace the air bag for free.

issues.sym: Clunks or knocks, pulling to one side, or vague handling.
issues.why: Some brake, chassis and suspension bolts weren't tightened enough at the factory (NHTSA 25V-434).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If you hear new clunks, get it inspected before driving far.

issues.t: Rear seat belts may not lock for child seats (recall)
issues.sym: A rear seat belt doesn't lock when pulled all the way out, so a child seat can loosen.
issues.why: Some rear belts were missing the automatic locking feature or could switch it off too early (NHTSA 21V-607 and 21V-606).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls; dealers replace the belts for free. Use the LATCH anchors for child seats until then.

issues.sym: Poor night visibility or other drivers flashing you because your headlights glare.
issues.why: Caps were put on the wrong headlight adjusters at the factory, so the beams could be misaimed (NHTSA 21V-413).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls; dealers fix the caps and aim for free.
